overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice for its August 29 meeting; it did not violate the law on discussion beyond the notice or on proposing release of executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: The August 29 notice listed a financial-interest disclosure topic under G.L. c. 268A §19, allegedly too vague to signal that the chiefs' Flea Market details would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Without more, a reasonable member of the public could not have read the topic and understood that the anticipated discussion would relate to Chief Kuss and Chief Contois working paid details at the Brimfield Flea Market.

allegations.summary: The Board allegedly discussed topics not listed on the August 29 notice, namely Chief Kuss's outstanding tasks and records requests.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we are satisfied that the Board’s discussion of outstanding work responsibilities naturally flowed from its consideration of the financial interest disclosure topic.

allegations.summary: A member allegedly threatened to reveal details of a June 30 executive session with the police chief by proposing release of those minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the disclosure of information or matters discussed in executive session or the release of executive session minutes sooner than required will not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
